lesson_title: Heat It, Cool It, Change It
hook_text: An ice lolly, a pot of boiling water and a sweaty glass of cool drink. One material, three changes.
clip_script: Hot day in Upington! The ice lolly drips. Heating makes a solid melt. Into the freezer goes a tray of water. Cooling makes a liquid freeze. Mom boils water for pap. Heating makes a liquid evaporate into invisible water vapour. Lift the lid. Drops! Cooling makes the vapour condense. And that cold glass of cool drink? It is not leaking. Water vapour from the air condensed on it. Melt, freeze, evaporate, condense. Same water, four changes.
visual_style: Whiteboard arrows going round a loop: ice to water to vapour when heated, and back again when cooled, with an ice lolly, a pot and a cold glass beside each step.
mood: Bright and summery, with a few cool surprises.
pacing: Melting and freezing first, then evaporating and condensing, then the loop that ties them together.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look for condensing on a cold glass at home.
